records.speaker: Villager
records.source_meaning: Resident of the village who recognizes fellow believers and entrusts their inherited lamp to those seeking the Proof.
records.localization_note: Villager identifies the resident who speaks for the community in this exchange. Neither the greeting nor the handover supplies a clerical or civic title.
records.context: SC3_B89 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Villager
records.source_meaning: Resident who asks where the fleet came from and proposes a trade for a sextant.
records.localization_note: Villager fits the local speaker’s curiosity and offer in both routes. Being willing to trade an object doesn’t make this a merchant or an official.
records.context: SC0_B339, SC3_B299 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Boy
records.source_meaning: The child Cristina tries to rescue from the sea. He thanks her and asks for the man who got them both to safety.
records.localization_note: Boy is an ordinary, clear label for the child. The boy’s mother and rescuers are identified by what they say and do.
records.context: SC3_B58 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Boy
records.source_meaning: A drowning child calls for his grandfather, then cries in relief and later says goodbye.
records.localization_note: Boy suits the child in both routes. The dialogue explicitly establishes whose grandson he is, and the short header reads naturally during the rescue.
records.context: SC0_B121, SC3_B95 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Lady
records.source_meaning: A woman whose polished speech marks social refinement. She praises home baking, talks fashion and takes an interest in how her friend cooked.
records.localization_note: Lady suits the polite social register across these towns without assigning the speaker a titled family or making this a single named person.
records.context: SC3_B151, SC3_B153, SC3_B154, SC3_B155, SC3_B166 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Lady
records.source_meaning: The second lady in the trend conversations. A separate London scene uses this label for the mother of the boy Cristina tries to rescue.
records.localization_note: Lady works as a reusable social label. Her husband in the bread exchange and the mother-son relationship in London belong to their respective scenes.
records.context: SC3_B58, SC3_B151, SC3_B153, SC3_B154, SC3_B155, SC3_B166 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Lady
records.source_meaning: The third lady expresses curiosity about bread and the ruby and offers to show her friends how she cooks with chili peppers.
records.localization_note: Lady fits the shared register with the other two speakers. She takes turns asking and teaching, so an occupational label would misidentify her.
records.context: SC3_B151, SC3_B154, SC3_B166 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Alluring Woman
records.source_meaning: An alluring woman approaches Ian, flirts as she offers an Indian book, and vanishes after offering it to him if he cannot pay.
records.localization_note: Alluring Woman captures her flirtatious manner and the scene’s mysterious tone. Ian only wonders whether she was a celestial maiden.
records.context: SC3_B170 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Mysterious Old Man
records.source_meaning: An unnamed older man appears in distinct scenes, asking for his grandson’s rescue in one and revealing an inherited prophecy in another.
records.localization_note: Mysterious Old Man reads as an anonymous story role. The rescue and prophecy convey their own relationships and give no reason to merge the people behind the shared label.
records.context: SC3_B95, SC3_B186 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Research Student
records.source_meaning: A research student who explains how a Dutch polder settlement has grown and tells Lil about the government’s demand for gold.
records.localization_note: Research Student is a natural designation for a student doing research. The polder project supplies no degree, university appointment or government title.
records.context: SC2_B39 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Owner
records.source_meaning: The establishment’s owner tastes the dish, insists customers want a sweeter flavor and leaves the method to the cook.
records.localization_note: Owner fits her authority over the food and her concern for the customers. It leaves the cook’s craft and the type of establishment to the scene.
records.context: SC3_B159 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Cook
records.source_meaning: The cook listens to the owner’s feedback, questions the change and asks how she wants the dish made sweeter.
records.localization_note: Cook is natural above these terse replies and matches the culinary job. The exchange establishes no kitchen hierarchy beyond who owns the place and who cooks.
records.context: SC3_B159 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Privateers
records.source_meaning: A speaker from the privateering fleet laughs at the young admiral and expects his fleet to be easy prey.
records.localization_note: Privateers reads naturally as a collective header over a single voice speaking for the opposing fleet. The crew calls them pirates in the dialogue, while the Japanese header names their distinct maritime role.
records.context: SC0_B20 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Sect Leader
records.source_meaning: The leader declares the research society’s revelation, commands the raid and demands protection when his followers scatter.
records.localization_note: Sect Leader conveys his authority within this belief group and suits a neutral header. The society’s chosen name and the crew’s mocking description can coexist in the exchange.
records.context: SC3_B88 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Villager
records.source_meaning: The village resident recognizes the discovery’s significance to the tribe and offers the dagger to the people who found it.
records.localization_note: Villager is an appropriate role for the local person who explains what was found. Speaking about the tribe and its spiritual life gives no basis for a title such as elder or priest.
records.context: SC3_B100 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Bandit
records.source_meaning: One of the raiders near São Jorge defends their motives, hears Maria out and ultimately agrees to sail with her.
records.localization_note: Bandit matches the role Maria challenges at the start of this exchange. His account of the harm done to his village and his eventual decision belong in the dialogue.
records.context: SC3_B97 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references

records.speaker: Explorer
records.source_meaning: The treasure seeker rejoices when the curse lifts and is relieved that the group can go home alive.
records.localization_note: Explorer fits a person who came looking for treasure and speaks about leaving alive. The exchange gives the group no formal profession or rank beyond the original role label.
records.context: SC0_B318 with exact speaker turns in exchange_references
